beats.beat: The company's product portfolio includes four categories: Functional Additives (FA), Chemically Modified Minerals (CMM), Soft Minerals (SM), and Hard Minerals (HM). These are specialty chemicals used across industries such as paints, plastics, construction, and personal care.

The company does not have its own sales and marketing team for most products; instead, it relies on a long-term arrangement with 20 Microns Limited, its corporate promoter, to market and sell the products. This is listed as a key competitive strength.

Customer concentration is high: the top 10 customers accounted for 59%, 57%, and 59% of revenue from operations in FY2017, FY2016, and FY2015 respectively. No long-term or definitive agreements exist with customers — business is conducted via purchase orders.
The company has export revenue, with shipments to Nigeria, Saudi Arabia, and Sri Lanka. Total exports over the past five years amounted to ₹1,068.18 lakh (₹10.68 crore).

beats.beat: The company has reported net profit for the last three full financial years, after making losses in FY2013 and FY2014. Profit after tax (PAT) stood at ₹1.49 crore in FY2015, ₹0.90 crore in FY2016, and ₹1.75 crore in FY2017. For the six months ending September 30, 2017, PAT was ₹1.33 crore.

Basic earnings per share (EPS) followed the same trajectory: ₹(0.45) in FY2013, ₹(0.20) in FY2014, ₹2.47 in FY2015, ₹1.46 in FY2016, ₹2.43 in FY2017, and ₹1.48 for the six-month period ended September 2017.

Operating cash flow was negative in only one of the six reported periods — FY2014 (‑₹3.50 crore) — and positive in all other periods, with FY2015 showing a strong inflow of ₹8.03 crore. For the six months ending September 2017, operating cash flow was ₹2.01 crore.
As of September 30, 2017, total assets were ₹30.19 crore. The company has contingent liabilities of ₹29.11 lakh as disclosed in the notes to the financial statements.

beats.beat: The company is promoted by Mr. Chandresh S. Parikh, Mr. Atil C. Parikh, Mr. Rajesh C. Parikh, and 20 Microns Limited (the corporate promoter). Together they hold 89,48,270 equity shares, representing 99.76% of the pre-issue paid-up capital. The remaining 0.24% is held by the promoter group excluding the promoters.

The company has entered into related-party transactions in each of the last five financial years and the six months ended September 30, 2017. Details are provided in the financial statements as per Accounting Standard 18.
The DRHP acknowledges past instances of non‑filing or incorrect filing of statutory forms with the Registrar of Companies (RoC), which were subsequently filed with additional fees.

One of the company's manufacturing facilities (Plot 9-10, GIDC Waghodia, Vadodara) does not yet have all required statutory licenses and registrations. The company warns it could be penalised for non-compliance.
The company has not obtained trademark registration for its corporate logo.

beats.beat: The Indian specialty chemicals market (excluding agrochemicals and dyestuff) was estimated at ₹1,000 billion (₹1 lakh crore) in fiscal 2017, according to CRISIL Research cited in the DRHP.

The segment grew at 10–12% CAGR from fiscal 2014 to 2017, and is forecast to grow at 12–14% CAGR going forward. Sub-segments such as construction chemicals, water chemicals, and personal care ingredients are expected to grow at 15% CAGR.
The industry is highly fragmented: small and medium enterprises (SMEs) hold 70–75% market share. Only a few domestic players have the scale to compete globally, but global giants are present.

Key growth drivers include rising consumption, urbanisation (urban population expected to reach 36% by 2020), government support (100% FDI allowed, Draft National Chemical Policy), and favourable global shifts as China tightens environmental norms on chemical manufacturing.

Regulations impacting the industry include REACH compliance for exports to Europe, GST implementation from July 2017, and the establishment of Petroleum, Chemicals and Petrochemicals Investment Regions (PCPIRs) in four states.

beats.beat: 20 Microns Nano Minerals Limited processes and sells specialty chemicals — specifically, Functional Additives, Chemically Modified Minerals, Soft Minerals, and Hard Minerals — to a range of industrial customers.

It has a long-term arrangement with its corporate promoter, 20 Microns Limited, which handles marketing and sales through its network. The company derives substantial synergies from this relationship.

The company is raising money through an IPO on the SME platform of NSE (NSE EMERGE) to fund capital expenditure and for general corporate purposes. The lead manager is Vivro Financial Services Private Limited.

intro.purpose: Orient the reader: who the company is, what it does, what it is raising and why it matters.

beats.beat: The IPO is a fresh issue of equity shares (no offer for sale). The exact number of shares and price band are not disclosed in the draft red herring prospectus.
The lead manager to the issue is Vivro Financial Services Private Limited.
The registrar is Link Intime India Private Limited.

Proceeds from the fresh issue will be used for: (1) capital expenditure to set up a new manufacturing facility at Plot 336, GIDC Waghodia, Vadodara, Gujarat; (2) general corporate purposes; and (3) listing of equity shares on NSE EMERGE to create a public market and enhance visibility. Specific amounts allocated to each object are not disclosed.

beats.beat: No long‑term customer or supplier agreements. The company operates on purchase orders and has no guaranteed volumes or pricing, which exposes revenue and margins to sudden changes in demand or input costs.
Missing statutory licenses for one manufacturing facility. If penalised or forced to halt operations, it could disrupt a significant part of production.
Past regulatory non‑compliance. Instances of late or incorrect filings with the RoC suggest weak compliance processes, which could attract penalties or regulatory scrutiny.
Negative operating cash flow in FY2014 (‑₹3.50 crore). While later years were positive, the earlier cash crunch indicates vulnerability during periods of low demand or high working capital needs.
Extreme promoter concentration: 99.76% pre‑issue. Post‑issue, promoter holding will remain very high, giving them near‑complete control and limited minority influence.
